result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers agree that a forced day-one tour is wrong for these users, and both propose inline shortcut hints, nudges triggered by repeated mouse use, a searchable reference grouped by task, and an A/B test to settle it with the PM. B is a little tighter. It also says plainly how to pick the day-one set (match the first-session workflow, then check against usage data) and offers the full walkthrough only as an opt-in track. A is thorough but longer, with more sections and more side points. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers agree with the user and recommend contextual hints, shortcuts shown in menus and tooltips, a searchable reference, and an A/B test to bring to the PM. B gives clearer reasons tied to this audience (billable time, existing habits, needing a real task before a shortcut sticks). B also drops the walkthrough entirely in favor of learning on a real first task, while A keeps a short day-one tour and adds an optional power-user track. A is a little more compact and is more explicit about picking the first few shortcuts from the first-session workflow, but neither answer is short.
